analysis.tooBig: Not enough free space: {size} to send, {free} free at the destination.
analysis.scanErrors: {n} item could not be read | {n} items could not be read
analysis.reopened: Transfer reopened from the list: the counts are the saved ones.

analysis.intro: filebridge counts the files and checks whether any name would cause problems at the destination. Nothing has been copied yet.
analysis.countingHint: Large folders can take a few minutes. You can wait here or come back later.
analysis.errorHint: Check that the files and the destination are still reachable, then try again.
analysis.guidePendingTitle: {n} name needs your decision | {n} names need your decision
analysis.guidePending: Accept the suggested fixes in one click: they are the safe choice and only change the copy. Or review them one by one.
analysis.guideOk: All good: no name needs changing. Click “Next” to review and send.
analysis.guideFixed: All good: the names below are adjusted automatically in the copy so the destination accepts them. Your originals keep their names. Click “Next”.
analysis.tooBigHint: There isn't enough free space at the destination. Free some space there, or go back and choose fewer files.
analysis.symlinksHelp: Shortcuts (symbolic links) point to other files. They aren't copied, so the same thing isn't copied twice and nothing outside the chosen folders gets in.
analysis.scanErrorsHelp: Usually files you don't have permission to read, or that were removed while counting. They won't be copied.
analysis.preflightHelp: whether the destination is reachable, accepts writing, and how much space is free
analysis.namesHelp: Some systems refuse certain names (Windows, for example, refuses “:” and “?”). filebridge fixes the name only in the copy; the original file stays as it is.
analysis.waitHint: Wait for the analysis to finish.
analysis.guideLook: These names need you to read them before deciding. Open each group and choose.
analysis.notBulk: {n} name is left for you to read first: garbled names and names without a suggestion are never accepted in one click. | {n} names are left for you to read first: garbled names and names without a suggestion are never accepted in one click.
analysis.acceptSuggestions: Accept the suggestion | Accept the {n} suggestions
analysis.repairHint: Earlier transfers to {destination} may have left garbled names like these there. Repair names, in its ⋮ menu in Destinations, fixes them where they are.

nfc.title: {n} name with accents stored differently | {n} names with accents stored differently
nfc.explain: Fixed automatically. The text looks the same, but the accents are stored in a way other systems may not recognise (common in files from a Mac). They're converted to the standard form (NFC).
nfc.example: “café.txt” looks the same before and after; only the hidden bytes change

nextcloud-nfc.title: {n} name Nextcloud would not find | {n} names Nextcloud would not find
nextcloud-nfc.explain: Fixed automatically. Nextcloud only finds names whose accents are stored in the standard form (NFC), so they're converted.
nextcloud-nfc.example: “Relatório.pdf” looks the same, but Nextcloud would not list it without the fix

forbidden-chars.title: {n} name with characters the destination refuses | {n} names with characters the destination refuses
forbidden-chars.explain: Fixed automatically. The destination doesn't accept < > : " \ {'|'} ? * or control characters in names; each one becomes _.

trailing.title: {n} name ending in a space or dot | {n} names ending in a space or dot
trailing.explain: Fixed automatically. Windows doesn't allow names that end in a space or a dot, so they're removed.

reserved.title: {n} reserved Windows name | {n} reserved Windows names
reserved.explain: Fixed automatically. Windows keeps some names for itself (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1…); they get a _ in front.

nextcloud-reserved.title: {n} name Nextcloud reserves | {n} names Nextcloud reserves
nextcloud-reserved.explain: Fixed automatically. Nextcloud keeps some names for itself, like .htaccess; they get a _ in front.

collision.title: {n} name that would clash with another | {n} names that would clash with another
collision.explain: After the fixes, two different names would end up the same at the destination, and one would replace the other. “Accept” adds a number to this one; or edit it.
collision.example: “Photo.jpg” and “photo.jpg” on a disk that doesn't tell capitals apart → “photo (2).jpg”

encoding.title: {n} name written in an old encoding | {n} names written in an old encoding
encoding.explain: These names were saved by an older system (often Windows), not as UTF-8, so other systems can't read them. filebridge reads them as Windows-1252 and sends the readable name; the bytes are shown so you can check. A name it could only guess waits for you.

mojibake.title: {n} garbled name | {n} garbled names
mojibake.explain: These names look like they were once read with the wrong encoding and saved that way, which turns accents into pairs like “Ã³”. “Accept” uses the repaired name, on the right. Check first: a real name can look like this, so it is never fixed by itself.

length.title: {n} name too long for the destination | {n} names too long for the destination
length.explain: The destination doesn't take names (or paths) this long, so these files would fail. “Accept” shortens the middle of the name and keeps its start, end and extension; or edit it, or skip it.
length.example: “Relatório anual de atividades da associação 2023.pdf” → “Relatório anual…ação 2023.pdf”

nextcloud.intro: filebridge connects over SSH either to the Proxmox host (and finds the Nextcloud container) or straight to the machine Nextcloud runs on, and checks each step. Nothing is changed during detection.
nextcloud.ncUserHint: The account that receives the files
nextcloud.folderHint: Empty = the top of that user's files
nextcloud.folderHostPath: This looks like a path on the server. Type a folder inside the Nextcloud user's files (e.g. Backup): filebridge finds the data folder by itself.
nextcloud.pickContainer: More than one container looks like Nextcloud. Which one?

runtime.proxmox-lxc: Nextcloud runs in a container on this Proxmox host.
runtime.host: Nextcloud runs on this machine itself (no Proxmox container).
runtime.docker: Nextcloud runs in a Docker container on this machine (the official image or Nextcloud AIO).
runtime.snap: Nextcloud runs as a snap on this machine.

nextcloud.advancedHint: only if the detection asks for it
nextcloud.detectTip: Connects and checks everything, step by step. Nothing is changed on the server.

help.ncUser: The Nextcloud account that receives the files: the login name, not the display name.
help.host: The address of the Proxmox node that runs the Nextcloud container, or of the machine Nextcloud runs on (its container, VM or server, e.g. its Tailscale address).
help.sshUser: The user filebridge logs in with over SSH on that server. Files are written as this user, so it must be able to write to Nextcloud's data folder: in practice, root.
help.folder: A folder inside that user's files. Empty puts the files at the top.
help.ctid: Proxmox only: the number of the container where Nextcloud runs. Leave empty and filebridge finds it.
help.installDir: Where Nextcloud is installed inside the container. Leave empty and filebridge finds it.
help.dedicated: Instead of root, filebridge signs in as a user of its own: in the web server's group (so it can hand the files it sends to Nextcloud without root), allowed by one sudoers line to run only Nextcloud's occ. filebridge shows the commands to set this up; you run them yourself.
help.sshPassword: A phone has no SSH agent. filebridge signs in once with this password, adds its own key to the SSH user's authorized_keys (restricted, removable with Remove access) and from then on signs in only with that key. The password is never kept.

hint.host: The Proxmox node or the Nextcloud server itself
hint.sshPassword: Used once to install filebridge's own key on the server, then forgotten.

advice.title: Not sure which to pick? Let filebridge check the server
advice.intro: filebridge signs in over SSH and looks for Nextcloud as direct mode would, then recommends a mode. Nothing is changed on the server and nothing is saved.
advice.ready: SSH reaches the machine Nextcloud runs on with the rights direct mode needs, so big sends can go straight into its data folder.
advice.unreachable: SSH did not connect to this server, so direct mode can't work from here. WebDAV needs only Nextcloud's address and an app password.
advice.rights: Nextcloud is there, but this SSH user lacks the rights direct mode needs (root or passwordless sudo, and writing the user's files folder). WebDAV needs none of that.
advice.not_found: No usable Nextcloud was found on this server over SSH. WebDAV needs only Nextcloud's address and an app password.
advice.untrusted: The server's key was not trusted, so filebridge did not sign in. WebDAV needs only Nextcloud's address and an app password.
advice.override: You can still pick the other mode above.

nextcloud.dedicatedHint: Use that user as the SSH user. It signs in to the machine Nextcloud runs on (not the Proxmox node).
nextcloud.serverSetup: Server setup for the dedicated user
nextcloud.serverSetupHint: filebridge never runs these and never changes sudoers. Read them, run them yourself as root on the server, then press Detect again.

immich.intro: filebridge copies the files into a folder of an Immich external library (over SFTP, or into a folder of this computer), then asks Immich to scan that library. Immich only reads the folder: it never moves or deletes your files.
immich.via: How files reach the library's folder

viaHint.sftp: The server that holds Immich's library folder (a NAS, or the Immich machine itself), reached over SSH.
viaHint.local: Immich reads a folder of this computer, or of a disk mounted here.

immich.importPath: This folder as Immich sees it
immich.https: Use https://: the API key must not travel unencrypted.
immich.pickLibrary: Immich's libraries: pick the one for this folder and check again (or fix the folder).
immich.sameFolderFail: Immich doesn't see the files sent to {folder}: a test file written there wasn't in “{importPath}” as Immich sees it. If Immich runs in Docker, type in “This folder as Immich sees it” the path its container uses for this folder; otherwise send to the folder the library imports. (The test file was removed.)

help.server: The address where Immich opens in the browser, e.g. photos.example.com. It must use https:// (for example behind a reverse proxy with a certificate); plain http:// works only on this computer.
help.apiKey: Create one in Immich, signed in as an administrator: Account settings → API keys → New API key. Give it at least library.read, library.update and queue.read (job.read before Immich 2), or all permissions. filebridge keeps it in the system keyring.
help.importPath: If Immich runs in Docker, it sees the folder under another path (e.g. /mnt/photos for /srv/photos on the server): type that path here. Empty = the same path as the folder above.
help.library: The external library that imports this folder (Administration → External libraries). Empty = filebridge finds it by the folder.

hint.apiKey: Kept in the system keyring, not in filebridge.
hint.importPath: Empty = the same as the folder above

settings.title: Settings
settings.notificationsHint: System notification when a transfer finishes or fails.
settings.autostart: Start the engine when I log in
settings.autostartHint: The copy engine starts by itself each time you log in, so unfinished sends continue without opening filebridge.

autostartWhy.app_image: Not available while filebridge runs from an AppImage. Install the .deb or .rpm package to use it.
autostartWhy.no_service: filebridge-service was not found next to the app, so this can't be set up.
autostartWhy.no_systemd: Needs a systemd user session, which this computer doesn't have.
autostartWhy.no_launchd: Needs to run in your macOS desktop session, where launchd starts it at login.

settings.autostartOutdated: It is set to start another copy of the engine. Update it to start this one ({exec}).

autostartOn.title: Start the engine when you log in?

write.systemd_unit: Writes {path}, which tells systemd to run {exec} each time you log in.
write.launch_agent: Writes {path}, which tells macOS (launchd) to run {exec} each time you log in.
write.run_key: Adds {path} to the Windows registry, which runs {exec} each time you log in. It starts the copy engine without opening a window.

autostartOn.login: From your next login the copy engine runs before you open filebridge, and unfinished sends continue by themselves.
autostartOn.now: The copy engine running now keeps running: nothing stops.
autostartOn.undo: You can turn it off here at any time.
autostartOn.agentPinned: It also tells the engine where your SSH agent is, so destinations that sign in with it keep working.
autostartOn.agentMissing: Your SSH agent moves at each login, so the engine started this way can't reach it: SFTP and Nextcloud destinations that sign in with it will fail. Give them filebridge's own key (Destinations), or open filebridge before they send.

autostartOff.title: Stop starting the engine when you log in?

remove.systemd_unit: Turns it off in systemd and deletes {path}.
remove.launch_agent: Stops it in launchd and deletes {path}.

autostartOff.login: From your next login the copy engine starts only when you open filebridge.

now.systemd_unit: If systemd started the copy engine running now, it stops and filebridge starts it again at once: running sends pause for a moment and continue.
now.launch_agent: If launchd started the copy engine running now, it stops and filebridge starts it again at once: running sends pause for a moment and continue.
now.run_key: The copy engine running now keeps running: nothing stops.

settings.overnight: Crosses midnight: from {start} today until {end} the next day.
settings.sendingHint: Applies to every transfer, including the ones already running. Times are this computer's local time; the computer has to be on and awake when the hours start.
settings.badLimit: Enter a speed greater than zero.
settings.badWindow: Start and end must be different times.
settings.serviceHint: filebridge-service does the transfers; the window only shows them. It starts by itself when needed.
settings.copyLogHint: For bug reports: the engine's recent messages, without passwords or keys.
settings.logEmpty: The engine hasn't logged anything yet.
settings.bandwidthHelp: The most filebridge may use of your connection, so the internet stays fast for everything else.
settings.scheduleHelp: The hours when transfers may run, for example only at night.
settings.themeHint: System follows your computer's light or dark mode.
settings.guidesHint: A short tour the first time you open a screen. The ? next to a title plays it again.
settings.guidesResetDone: Every guide will show again the next time.
settings.intro: Changes are saved as you make them.

skip.restart: The other files being sent right now start again from the beginning.
skip.stays: It stays marked as skipped in the file list and the report, so its folder can't be shown as safe to free. A new transfer or Send again can send it later.

composition.noTotal: This destination doesn't report its total size.
composition.noFree: This destination doesn't report its free space.

again.title: Send again: {name}
again.explain: Only files that are new or changed since the last time will travel; files already there and identical are skipped.
again.decisions: Name decisions you made last time are reused.
again.noDelete: Nothing is deleted at the destination, even files removed from the source since.
again.otherRules: Another destination may check names differently.

activity.sentWarnings: Sent to {destination}, with {n} warning | Sent to {destination}, with {n} warnings
activity.empty: Nothing happened yet. What your transfers do, even with the window closed, appears here.

report.title: Export report
report.private: The report names the destination and its folder, never the server's address, user or keys.
report.sealed: Sealed — JSON plus a readable HTML copy; any later change shows when checked
report.sealedHint: Two files: the .json is the proof, the .html opens in any browser. Every entry is chained into one SHA-256 code, so “Check a report…” (or filebridge report check) shows any later change.
report.keepSeal: Keep this code somewhere else (an email, a note): later it proves both files unchanged.

check.title: Check a sealed report
check.intro: Pick the .json or the .html of a sealed report: filebridge checks both against their seal.
check.intact: Intact: {n} entry, exactly as exported | Intact: {n} entries, exactly as exported
check.noCopy: There is no readable .html copy beside it.
check.compare: Compare it with the code you kept elsewhere: if they match, nobody rewrote the files and their seal.

problem.unreadable: Not readable as a filebridge report: {detail}
problem.not_sealed: Exported without a seal: there is nothing to check. Export it again as “Sealed”.
problem.header: The summary at the top was changed.
problem.entry: Entry {n} ({path}) was changed, or one just before it was removed or added.
problem.seal: Entries were removed or added at the end, or the seal itself was changed.
problem.readable: The readable .html copy doesn't match the .json.

compare.title: Compare reports
compare.intro: What changed from one finished transfer to another. Files are matched by their path at the source.
compare.pickSecond: Choose the transfer to compare with.
compare.otherSources: These transfers have different source folders: files with the same path may not be the same files.
compare.otherDestination: These transfers went to different destinations.
compare.same: No differences: both reports say the same.

reclaim.title: Space you can free at the source
reclaim.notYet: Freeing the source isn't safe yet
reclaim.body: All {files} files of this transfer arrived and were verified identical at {destination} on {date}. Nothing changed at the source since
reclaim.never: filebridge never deletes anything. If you want the space back, delete these folders yourself, in your file manager.
reclaim.sizeOnly: Compared by size only (transfer from an older version).
reclaim.changedList: Files new or changed at the source
reclaim.notice: You can free {size} at the source.

blocker.not_verified: Verification was off for this transfer.

blocker.not_checked: The source hasn't been checked since the transfer.

blocker.source_unavailable: The source isn't there now. Connect the disk to check it.

browse.title: Choose a folder on {destination}
browse.truncated: Showing the first {n}. Type the start of a name and press Enter to find the rest.

dest.lastUsed: same as the last transfer here

home.title: Home

headline.needsYou: {n} transfer needs you | {n} transfers need you
headline.sending: {n} transfer is sending | {n} transfers are sending

home.drop: Drop folders here to start a transfer
home.reclaimTotal: You can free {size} at the source.

offline.title: Your transfers show here once the copy engine answers.
offline.body: Nothing is lost meanwhile: the transfers and destinations are kept by the engine, not by this window.

welcome.title: Copy without losing anything. And prove that everything arrived.
welcome.noDestination: You'll choose where the copy goes on the way: a disk, a server or Nextcloud.

source.title: Your originals are never touched
source.body: Nothing at the source is deleted, moved or renamed.

names.title: Names arrive right
names.body: Accents, forbidden characters and garbled names are fixed in the copy only.

proof.title: Proof that it all arrived
proof.body: Every file checked by SHA-256, with a report you can keep.

home.pausedByYou: Paused. It continues from the same point when you resume it.

tour.replay: Show the guide for this step

steps.title: Send in {n} steps
steps.body: Choose what to send, then where. filebridge checks every name, you review, and the copy starts. You can go back to an earlier step until you send.

add.title: Add what you want to send
add.body: Drag files and folders onto the window, or use the buttons. Add as many as you like: they all go to the same place, and nothing at the source changes.

recent.title: The same place again
recent.body: Folders you sent before are here: one click adds one. One on a disk that isn't plugged in shows as not found.

chosen.title: Check what you chose
chosen.body: Each item says what it is and how big. If one can't be sent (missing, a link, or already inside another folder) it says why, with a fix.

next.title: Then choose where it goes
next.body: Next is ready once there is nothing to fix. The files are counted after you choose the destination.

summary.title: What you're sending
summary.body: Every file was counted, and the destination checked: it can be reached, accepts writing and has room. Nothing has been copied yet.

decide.title: Decide in one click
decide.body: The suggested fixes are the safe choice: they change the name only in the copy. Accept them all here, or review them one by one.

names.title: Names the destination wouldn't take
names.body: Each group is one reason, with an example. Open a group to see every name and choose for each one: accept, keep, skip or edit.

next.title: Then review and send
next.body: Next is ready once every name is decided. You can still come back here before sending.

card.title: One card per destination
card.body: Where it is, how much space is left, and which names its file system refuses. Saved once, picked in every transfer.

actions.title: Test, browse, and the rest
actions.body: Test checks that filebridge can reach it and write; Browse shows its folders. The ⋮ menu edits it, repairs names already there, or deletes it (never its files).

new.title: Another place to copy to
new.body: An external disk, a server over SSH, or Nextcloud. Each one is checked before it is saved.

repair.title: Repair names at the destination
repair.lead: Names already in {folder} on {destination}, checked with the same rules as a transfer. Nothing is renamed until you confirm.
repair.label: Repair · {folder}
repair.buttonTip: Check the names already in a folder of this destination and fix them there
repair.readCount: {n} file so far | {n} files so far
repair.cleanBody: {n} file checked; nothing to rename. | {n} files checked; nothing to rename.
repair.howTo: These names would change. Decide the ones marked pending; “Skip” leaves a name (and, for a folder, what's inside) as it is.
repair.pending: Decide {n} name first | Decide {n} names first

confirm.title: Rename {n} name? | Rename {n} names?
confirm.onlyNames: Files are not copied, changed or deleted: only renamed. The old names stay in this repair's report.
confirm.taken: A new name that is already taken is left as it was and reported.
confirm.nextcloud: Nextcloud then rescans the folders that changed, so it shows the new names.
confirm.immich: Immich then scans the library. It sees each renamed file as a new photo: the old entry goes offline, and its albums, favourites and descriptions don't move to the new one.

modeHint.webdav: Recommended: needs only Nextcloud's address and an app password, works from anywhere, and Nextcloud indexes the files as they arrive.
modeHint.direct: For big first migrations on your own network: writes straight into Nextcloud's data folder over SSH, then asks Nextcloud to index what arrived.

webdav.intro: filebridge signs in to Nextcloud with an app password, like the desktop and phone apps do. Nothing needs to be set up on the server.
webdav.https: Use https://: an app password must not travel unencrypted. If the server is at home, you can allow http:// above.
webdav.plainHttp: Allow http:// (the server is on my home network or Tailscale)
webdav.plainHttpWarn: Unencrypted: the app password and your files travel in clear on your network. Accepted only when the address is at home or on Tailscale.
webdav.ipAddress: An IP address rarely works with https://: the certificate is made for the server's name. Enter the name you open Nextcloud with in the browser, or trust the server's certificate below.
webdav.trustCertificateHint: For your own server with a self-signed certificate (or one made for another name). Still encrypted, but filebridge no longer checks that the server is really yours: tick it only for a server you know.
webdav.trustCertificateAgain: The server's certificate was refused. If this is your own server, tick “Trust this server's certificate” above and check again.

help.server: The address you open Nextcloud at in the browser, e.g. cloud.example.com. A WebDAV address copied from Nextcloud's Files settings works too, and is needed when you sign in with an email address or a company account.
help.appPassword: Create one in Nextcloud: Settings → Security → Devices & sessions → “Create new app password”. It can be revoked there at any time, and it is not your account password. filebridge keeps it in the system keyring.
help.folder: Where transfers go, inside the user's files, e.g. Backup/Fotos. It is created by the first transfer if it doesn't exist.

webdav.appPasswordHint: Not the password you sign in to Nextcloud with: with two-factor sign-in that one can't work here. Create one in Nextcloud under Settings → Security → Devices & sessions.
webdav.appPasswordShort: This is shorter than any Nextcloud app password (they look like xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx): it is probably the password you sign in with.

access.uses: Signs in with filebridge's own key

install.tip: Give this destination a key of its own, kept in the system keyring, so your personal SSH key is no longer used
install.title: Use filebridge's own key for “{name}”?
install.what1: filebridge makes a new key on this computer and keeps it in the system keyring, never in a file.
install.what2: It adds one line to the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {who}, marked “restrict”: no interactive terminal, no tunnels, no forwarding. Nothing else on the server changes.
install.what3: From then on this destination signs in with that key instead of yours; your key stays where it is.
install.what4: It signs in with the new key before switching. If any step fails, everything is undone.
install.ok: Done: this destination now uses filebridge's own key.
install.unconfirmed: Installed, but not every check could be made: see the steps marked !.
install.failed: Not installed: each step below says what was undone.
install.failedUndo: Not installed, and the undo didn't finish: see the steps marked ✗ for what is left.

remove.tip: Delete filebridge's key from the server and the keyring, and check that it no longer signs in
remove.title: Remove filebridge's access to “{name}”?
remove.what1: filebridge deletes its own line from the ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {who}, and nothing else.
remove.what2: It tries the old key once more and checks that the server refuses it; if the server still accepts it, nothing else changes.
remove.what3: Only then does this destination sign in with your key file or SSH agent again, if it has one.
remove.what3Password: Only then does this destination sign in with its password again.
remove.what4: Last, it deletes the key from the system keyring.
remove.ok: Done: filebridge's key is gone and no longer signs in.
remove.unconfirmed: Removed, but not everything could be confirmed: see the steps marked !.
remove.failed: Not finished: see the step that failed.

access.offer: Finished sending to “{name}”? When you won't send there again, remove filebridge's key from the server.

hostKey.title: Trust this server?
hostKey.intro: filebridge has not connected to {host} before. Check that this is really your server before going on: someone on the network could be pretending to be it.
hostKey.howToCheck: Compare it with the fingerprint the server shows: ask whoever runs it, or run this on the server. Trust it only if they are the same.
hostKey.savedIn: It will be added to {file}, and this server will not be asked about again.
hostKey.changed: {host} presented a different key from the one saved in {file} (line {line}). filebridge will not connect.
hostKey.changedWhat: Either the server was reinstalled or its keys were replaced, or someone is intercepting the connection. If whoever runs the server confirms the change, remove the old line from that file and try again.
hostKey.unreachable: Could not check the server's key: {error}

result.verified: file copied and verified, one by one | files copied and verified, one by one
result.noDifferences: No differences: every file at the destination is identical to its original (SHA-256).
result.notVerified: Verification was off for this transfer: the copies weren't read back and compared.
result.problems: of {n} file copied | of {n} files copied
result.problemsSub: {problems} file needs a look: it failed, or differs at the destination. | {problems} files need a look: they failed, or differ at the destination.
result.failed: of {n} file copied before the transfer stopped | of {n} files copied before the transfer stopped
result.cancelled: of {n} file copied before it was cancelled | of {n} files copied before it was cancelled
result.cancelledSub: What arrived stays at the destination; nothing was deleted anywhere.
result.renamed: {n} name fixed for the destination | {n} names fixed for the destination
result.retries: retried by itself once | retried by itself {n} times
result.notSent: Couldn't be sent, even after retrying each one:
result.reclaim: You can free {size} at the source.

help.host: The address of the computer or NAS that shares the folder: its name on the network or its IP address.
help.share: The shared folder's name: what comes after the server in \\server\name. On a NAS it is the shared folder you created (e.g. “backup”).
help.port: The SMB port. Leave 445 unless whoever set up the server told you otherwise.
help.user: The user you sign in to the share with. Empty signs in as the guest, for shares open to everyone.
help.domain: The user's domain or workgroup. Leave empty unless the server is in a Windows domain (most homes use WORKGROUP).
help.password: That user's password on the server. It is kept in your system's keyring (Keychain, Credential Manager, GNOME Keyring), never in filebridge's files.
help.folder: A folder inside the share where the copies go, with “/” between folders. It is created by the first send if it isn't there.

hint.folder: e.g. Fotos/2026; empty = straight into the share

s3.bucketSlash: Only the bucket's name here; the folder inside it goes in “Folder in the bucket”.
s3.pathStyle: Path-style addressing (MinIO and most self-hosted servers)
s3.https: Use https://: the requests are signed, but the files would travel unencrypted.

help.endpoint: The address of the S3 server, with https:// and its port if it has one. Leave empty for Amazon S3 (AWS).
help.region: The bucket's region, e.g. eu-west-1. On AWS it is shown next to the bucket; most self-hosted servers accept anything or leave it empty.
help.provider: Which server it is, so its particular ways are respected. If yours isn't listed, keep “Other / generic”.
help.bucket: The bucket the copies go into. It must exist already, or the key must be allowed to create it.
help.accessKeyId: The key's id, created in the server's console (AWS: IAM → Access keys; MinIO: Access Keys). It is not secret; the secret access key is.
help.secret: The key's secret, shown once when the key is created. It is kept in your system's keyring (Keychain, Credential Manager, GNOME Keyring), never in filebridge's files.
help.pathStyle: On: the address is server/bucket, which MinIO and most self-hosted servers need. Off: bucket.server, for AWS buckets and servers that ask for it.
help.folder: A folder inside the bucket where the copies go, with “/” between folders. S3 has no empty folders: it appears with the first file.

hint.accessKeyId: Empty = no key, for a public bucket
hint.folder: e.g. backup/fotos; empty = straight into the bucket

schedules.title: Scheduled sends
schedules.intro: A scheduled send runs on its own at the times you set, or whenever a folder changes, in the background engine, even with this window closed. Each run sends only what is new or changed since the last one.
schedules.empty: No scheduled sends yet. Create one to send a folder every night, every few hours, or whenever it changes.
schedules.emptyNoDestination: Add a destination first; then you can schedule sends to it.
schedules.notOnItsOwn: Switched off: runs only when you press Run now
schedules.nothingChanged: Nothing new or changed since the last run.

outcome.still_running: skipped: the previous run wasn't finished

when.hours: Every hour from {time} | Every {n} hours from {time}

remove.title: Remove this schedule?
remove.keepsRuns: Its earlier runs stay in Transfers.
remove.keepsFiles: Nothing is deleted at the source or at the destination.

form.name: Name
form.pickTitle: Choose what to send on schedule
form.fixed: What is sent and where can't change once saved: remove the schedule and create a new one.
form.localTime: In this computer's local time. If it is off or asleep at that time, the send runs once when it is back.
form.enabled: Run on its own at these times
form.onlyChanged: Each run sends only files that are new or changed since the last run.
form.keepsOlder: If a file changed, its older version at the destination is kept with the date in its name — nothing is overwritten.
form.waitsWindow: Runs wait for the send hours set in Settings, like any send.
form.needSources: Add at least one file or folder.
form.watchHelp: The background engine watches these folders and sends what changes once they have been quiet this long (at most 15 minutes after a change). It also checks the whole folder every hour, and when it starts.
form.enabledWatch: Watch and send on its own
form.neverDeletes: A file deleted or renamed here stays at the destination: nothing there is ever deleted.
form.stillWriting: A file still being written waits until it stops changing.
form.watchWindow: Outside the send hours set in Settings, changes wait and go together when they open.

watch.title: Watching
watch.limitHelp: This computer's limit on watched folders was reached; the folder is still sent, checked every 10 minutes. To watch it again, raise the limit and then save this schedule:
